skill.name: seedance-2-5-reference-to-video
skill.description: Generate 4-30 second 1080p videos from reference images, clips, and audio through RunComfy's Seedance 2.5 endpoint.
skill.summary: Create reference-guided Seedance 2.5 videos with consistent subjects, style, motion, and synchronized audio.
skill.author: genmedia-labs

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, links, example domains, and an abbreviated endpoint. Confirmed behavior includes package execution, scoped RunComfy commands, authentication, remote API traffic, and output downloads. User-controlled values embedded in single-quoted shell input create a high-confidence shell injection risk.

remediation.issue: User-controlled prompt text and URLs can break the single-quoted shell argument.
remediation.suggestion: Construct arguments with a process API that bypasses a shell, or apply complete shell escaping before execution. Test apostrophes, newlines, and shell metacharacters.

remediation.issue: The setup examples execute unpinned npm packages.
remediation.suggestion: Pin reviewed package versions and require explicit user approval before installation. Document how users can verify the package source and integrity.

remediation.issue: Generation sends user-selected data to a paid third-party service.
remediation.suggestion: Show the destination, estimated cost, and selected reference URLs before submission. Require confirmation when sensitive media or material costs are involved.

content.value_statement: Keeping characters, products, and visual style consistent across generated video is difficult. This skill builds and runs reference-guided Seedance 2.5 requests through RunComfy.
actual_capabilities: Builds Seedance 2.5 reference-to-video requests for RunComfy.
Accepts up to nine images, three videos, and three audio references.
Configures duration, aspect ratio, and synchronized audio generation.
Guides users through 480p drafts before 1080p delivery.
Explains counted-second pricing and recommends suitable related endpoints.
limitations: Output resolution is fixed at 1080p on the documented endpoint.
Duration is limited to 4-30 whole seconds.
The endpoint has no seed parameter, so repeated calls may differ.
Published schema and observed behavior disagree on whether a reference video is required.

use_cases.title: Maintain Character Identity
use_cases.description: Generate several shots that preserve a person's face, wardrobe, and visual treatment from supplied images.

use_cases.title: Create Product Motion Clips
use_cases.description: Combine product stills with a short motion reference to produce consistent promotional footage.

use_cases.title: Prototype Social Video
use_cases.description: Test references at 480p, select the best result, then render a vertical 1080p version.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Clip
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 5-second 16:9 video from [reference URL]. Show [subject] performing [action] with [lighting]. Do not add text or watermarks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with one clear reference and one simple action.

prompt_templates.title: Preserve a Character
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these identity and wardrobe images: [URLs]. Create an 8-second 9:16 shot where [character action]. Keep face, clothing, and colors consistent.
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a character-focused vertical clip from several still images.

prompt_templates.title: Match Product Motion
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [product image URLs] for geometry and [video URL] for camera motion. Generate a 6-second product shot with [background], [lighting], and [sound].
prompt_templates.scenario: Transfer camera rhythm while preserving product appearance.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Reference Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these image, video, and audio references: [URLs]. Recommend a 480p test plan, estimate counted seconds, then request approval before the 1080p render.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a cost-aware production workflow with multiple references.

output_examples.input: Three portrait references, one four-second handheld clip, an eight-second vertical output, and quiet street ambience.
output_examples.output: Prepared an eight-second vertical character shot using the portraits for identity and the clip for camera rhythm. Estimated counted duration: 12 seconds.

output_examples.input: Product front and side images, a turntable motion reference, and a clean studio background.
output_examples.output: Prepared a product-focused 1080p request with preserved geometry, matched turntable motion, controlled studio lighting, and no text.

output_examples.input: A moodboard and two candidate movement clips for a five-second brand video.
output_examples.output: Recommended separate 480p tests for each movement clip before selecting one reference stack for the final 1080p generation.

best_practices: Use images for stable identity, geometry, wardrobe, and brand colors.
Trim video references to the shortest segment that demonstrates the desired motion.
Test reference combinations at 480p before approving a 1080p render.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated visual styles in one reference stack.
Do not reuse Seedance 2.0 field names for this endpoint.
Do not submit sensitive references without reviewing the external service and destination.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It generates reference-guided 1080p Seedance 2.5 videos through RunComfy.

faq.question: Which reference types are supported?
faq.answer: The documented request supports images, video clips, and audio files through publicly reachable URLs.

faq.question: How long can the output be?
faq.answer: The output can be 4-30 seconds in whole-second steps.

faq.question: How is usage priced?
faq.answer: The documented 1080p rate is based on output duration plus total reference-video duration. Confirm current pricing before submission.

faq.question: Can it reproduce the exact same result?
faq.answer: No seed parameter is documented, so exact reproduction between calls is not guaranteed.

faq.question: Where are generated files saved?
faq.answer: The RunComfy CLI downloads completed files into the output directory chosen for the command.
